headline: Approved Certificate of Appropriateness for gutter, roof, and snow guard work at 28 West Broadway.
summary: Blackstone Restoration asked to replace gutters, valleys, and downspouts, the upper and bay window roofs, and install five snow guards. The site is in the Whitney Park Historic District. Commissioners found the plan met the city's historic preservation code, and they also adopted findings for 225 Cedar Street.
decisions: Approved the September 24, 2026 meeting minutes; all voting members in favor.
Adopted findings and decision for 225 Cedar Street; all voting members in favor.
Found that Commissioner Keebler does not have a conflict of interest; all voting members in favor.
Found the application for 28 West Broadway complete, a Certificate of Appropriateness, with all fees paid; all voting members in favor.
Found the 28 West Broadway project satisfies Historic Preservation Code §148-9A on alterations; all voting members in favor.
Deemed Part 2, Sections 1, 5-8, and Part 3 of the 28 West Broadway review not applicable; all voting members in favor.
Found the 28 West Broadway project satisfies Historic Preservation Code §148-9B(2)(b) on rehabilitation work; all voting members in favor.
Found the 28 West Broadway project satisfies Historic Preservation Code §148-9B(2)(c) on replacing deteriorated features; all voting members in favor.
Found the 28 West Broadway project satisfies Historic Preservation Code § 148-9B(2)(d) on distinctive features and craftsmanship; all voting members in favor.
Found the 28 West Broadway project satisfies Historic Preservation Code § 148-9B(2)(i) on removable alterations; all voting members in favor.
Approved Certificate of Appropriateness for the 28 West Broadway project; all voting members in favor.

73 HARLOW STREET

ommission Members Present:  Nathaniel King

ity Staff Present: Anja Collette, Planning Officer

air King called the meeting to order at 7:00 P.M. 
______________________________________________________________________

ld Business: 
1. Meeting Minutes – September 24, 2026
C
ommissioner Coe moved to approve the September 24th meeting minutes. Seconded by 
Commissioner Keebler. All voting members in favor, none opposed. Motion passed. 
2. Adoption of Findings & Decision for 225 Cedar Street
C
ommissioner Coe moved to adopt the findings and decisions for 225 Cedar Street. Seconded by 
Commissioner Keebler. All voting members in favor, none opposed. Motion passed. 
N
ew Business: 
1. C
ertificate of Appropriateness – 28 West Broadway – Map/Lot 022-065 – Applicant:
Blackstone Restoration – Owner: Stephen & Allison Freese – The applicant,
Blackstone Restoration, requests approval for Certificate of Appropriateness for the
replacement of gutter lines, valleys, and downspouts. Additionally, the applicant
Historic Preservation Commission – Meeting Minutes 
October 8th, 2026 
proposes the replacement of the upper roof and bay window roof, as well as the 
installation of five snow guards. The project is located at 28 West Broadway, Map-Lot 
022-065, in the Whitney Park Historic District. Applicant: Blackstone Restoration. Owner: 
Stephen & Allison Freese. 
 
Chair King introduced the agenda item. 
 
Commissioner Keebler brought forth a potential conflict of interest, as Blackstone Restoration rents a 
workshop space from him. Keebler did not believe it to be a conflict of interest as he has no financial 
holdings or influence in the company, but wanted to express it for consideration. Commissioner Coe did 
not find it to be a conflict. 
 
Commissioner Coe motioned that Commissioner Keebler does not have a conflict of interest. Seconded 
by Chair King. All voting members in favor, none opposed. Motion passed.  
 
Applicant Representative Matthew Weitkamp presented on the project on behalf of Blackstone 
Restoration and Stephen and Allison Freese. Weitkamp discussed the history of the home, sharing that 
architect C. Parker Crowell worked on the home for George E. Thompson in the colonial revival style.  
 
Applicant Representative Weitkamp provided an overview on metal corrosion issues and the proposed 
correctional work. He discussed replacing the steel lining in the wood gutters to copper and repairing 
damaged carpentry with in-kind mahogany materials. Weitkamp displayed samples of the materials. 
 
Applicant Representative Weitkamp discussed the proposal to replace the steel valleys and vent pipe 
with copper, install snow guards, and replace the EPDM roof. He shared the installation of copper 
downspouts and the replacement of slate hips and ridge.  
 
Applicant Representative Weitkamp provided an update on the previously approved carriage house 
project. 
 
HPC Consultant Pullen shared that C. Parker Crowell founded the firm now known as WBRC. He 
discussed that the question of what damaged carpentry will be repaired with mahogany was addressed 
in the presentation. Pullen asked whether the vertical curb is covered in metal or if it is painted wood – 
Applicant Representative Weitkamp responded that there is currently steel counter flasher that is to be 
replaced with copper. Pullen noted that the question of where the vent pipe replacement would occur 
had been addressed. 
 
Commissioner Keebler asked whether the steel gutters being replaced were original to the house -- 
Applicant Representative Weitkamp confirmed. Keebler asked wat the original material may have been 
on the EPDM – Weitkamp responded likely soldered zinc. Keebler asked about the choice surrounding 
the new EPDM material as opposed to copper – Weitkamp replied due to the cost and time-consuming 
nature of copper pans, as well as weather posing challenging expansion and contraction on solder 
joints. Keebler asked whether the steel edging is to be replaced with copper – Weitkamp confirmed. 
Keebler asked about the lifetime of the EPDM – Weitkamp responded that with maintenance, around 30 
to 40 years.  
 
Commissioner Keebler asked about the copper being soldered with lead and its longevity – Weitkamp 
responded the solder being used does not create a reactive situation with the copper. Keebler asked 
how effective the snow guards are – Weitkamp responded that when snow piles higher than the guards, 
it meters it in its fall.
Historic Preservation Commission – Meeting Minutes 
October 8th, 2026 
Commissioner Keebler asked about the possibility of the homeowners replacing the finials on the 
balustrade. 
 
Commissioner Keebler asked about the difference between the 16- and 20-ounce copper -- Applicant 
Representative Weitkamp responded that the 20-ounce copper choice is due to the extreme 
environment. Keebler and Weitkamp discussed the longevity of copper.  
 
Commissioner Coe asked whether the steel valleys are the dips in between connectors -- Applicant 
Representative Weitkamp provided a visual explanation. Coe discussed what would and would not be 
painted.  
 
Commissioner Keebler commented that it is a well-considered plan and he is pleased that homeowners 
are restoring their historic building. Commissioner Coe noted that she believes the copper downspouts 
will be a good addition. 
 
Chair King opened public comment – there were none. Public comment closed. 
 
Commissioner Keebler moved that the Commission finds the application was deemed complete on 
October 8, 2026, the proposed project is a Certificate of Appropriateness, and the applicant paid all 
applicable fees. Seconded by Commissioner Coe. All voting members in favor, none opposed. Motion 
passed. 
 
Commissioner Keebler moved that the Commissioner finds that, based on Exhibits 1-3, the application 
satisfied Historic Preservation Code §148-9A requiring that any alteration of the historic structure will 
preserve or enhance its historical and architectural character. Seconded by Commissioner Coe. All 
voting members in favor, none opposed. Motion passed. 
 
Commissioner Keebler moved that Part 2, Sections 1, 5-8, and Part 3 are deemed not applicable. 
Seconded by Commissioner Coe. All voting members in favor, none opposed. Motion passed. 
 
Commissioner Keebler moved that the Commission finds that, based on Exhibits 1-3, the application 
satisfies Historic Preservation Code § 148-9B(2)(b) requiring that rehabilitation work does not destroy 
the distinguishing qualities nor character of the structure and its environment. Seconded by 
Commissioner Coe. All voting members in favor, none opposed. Motion passed. 
 
Commissioner Keebler moved that the Commission finds that, based on Exhibits 1-3, the application 
satisfies Historic Preservation Code §148-9B(2)(c) requiring that, while repair is preferable to 
replacement, in the event that replacement of deteriorated architectural features is necessary, the 
feature being replaced in color, design, texture and other visual qualities and, where economically and 
technically feasible, materials. Seconded by Commissioner Coe. All voting members in favor, none 
opposed. Motion passed. 
 
Commissioner Keebler moved that the Commission finds that, based on Exhibits 1-3, the application 
satisfies Historic Preservation Code § 148-9B(2)(d) requiring that distinctive stylistic features or 
examples of skilled craftsmanship which characterize historic structures is not damaged or destroyed, 
wherever possible. Seconded by Commissioner Coe. All voting members in favor, none opposed. 
Motion passed. 
 
Commissioner Keebler moved that the Commission finds that, based on Exhibits 1-3, the application 
satisfies Historic Preservation Code § 148-9B(2)(i) requiring that, wherever possible, all alterations to 
structures shall be done in such a manner that if they were to be removed in the future the essential 
form and integrity of the original structure would be unimpaired. Seconded by Commissioner Coe. All

voting members in favor, none opposed. Motion passed. 
 
Commissioner Keebler moved that the Commission finds that, based on the findings in Parts 1-2 of 
Section IV of this document, the Project meets the requirements for a Certificate of Appropriateness and 
therefore grants a Certificate of Appropriateness for the proposed Project. Seconded by Commissioner 
Coe. All voting members in favor, none opposed. Motion passed. 
 
Planning Officer Collette reminded the Commission to share the upcoming vacancies on the Historic 
Preservation Commission with people they know.  
 
3. Adjournment 
 
Meeting adjourned at 7:33 PM.  
 
Respectfully submitted,  
 
Kayleigh Rienas 
Development Assistant 
Planning Division
